name: get-automations
description: Get Automations settings. section picks what to read. repos (the default): Release Autopilot account-wide auto-flagging and auto-releasing (the defaults a mapped repository inherits) and a page of repositories on the account's GitHub App install, each with mapped true or false and its project and effective settings when mapped. cleanup: a project's auto-cleanup settings and the flags its next run picks up. archival: a project's auto-archival settings (grace period, approvals, run limit, notifications), which get-projects does not return. cleanup and archival take projectKey and nothing else. For repos: mapped repositories not visible on the install are listed too, with visibleOnInstall false and no repo name. Pass repo (owner/name) or githubRepoId for one repository. Leave mapped unset to list connected and not-yet-connected repositories together; set it only when the user wants just one of the two groups. When hasMore is true, pass nextOffset as offset. When githubConnectUrl is present, GitHub is not connected: give that link to the user and retry after they finish. reposError means the install could not be read; retry later. For cleanup: auto-cleanup runs on a schedule and opens GitHub pull requests that remove the code for flags in the chosen flagStates, in the listed repositories; settings.schedule disabled means it is off, settings.configuredByMemberId is the member whose permissions cleanup jobs use, and upcoming.flagKeys and nextRunAt (Unix milliseconds) preview the next run. For archival: auto-archival archives flags that are ready to archive after graceSeconds, or creates approval requests when requireApproval is true; an error saying automatic archival is not available means the account does not have it yet. automationsPage links to the project's Automations page.

githubRepoId.description: Numeric GitHub repository id, an alternative to repo.

mapped.description: true lists only repositories mapped to a project; false only unmapped ones. Omit to list both.

offset.description: Pass nextOffset from the previous page.

projectKey.description: With section cleanup or archival: the project whose settings to read (required). Otherwise any LaunchDarkly project key, used to look up the account-wide GitHub App install; defaults to the oldest project.

repo.description: One GitHub repository's auto-flagging and auto-releasing, as owner/name, for example launchdarkly/gonfalon. Not for cleanup or archival.

section.description: repos (default): account auto-flagging and auto-releasing and the repositories. cleanup: one project's auto-cleanup settings and the flags its next run picks up. archival: one project's auto-archival settings. cleanup and archival require projectKey and take no other argument.

name: update-automations
description: Update Automations settings: Release Autopilot auto-flagging and auto-releasing, and a project's auto-cleanup and auto-archival (including turning either off). One change per call, in one of three forms. Account auto-flagging and auto-releasing: accountWide true. One repository's auto-flagging and auto-releasing: accountWide false with repo or githubRepoId, and projectKey on the first map. A project's auto-cleanup or auto-archival: projectKey with a cleanup or archival object, and no repo or githubRepoId; the repositories cleanup opens pull requests in go in cleanup.repositories. Send only what changed; omitted fields keep their stored values, and lists replace the whole list. approvalRequired applies only to auto-flagging. When githubConnectUrl is present, give that link to the user and retry after they finish. Saving cleanup makes the calling member the one whose permissions cleanup jobs use, and any schedule other than disabled makes LaunchDarkly open pull requests in the listed repositories, so confirm the schedule, repositories, and maxJobsPerRun with the user first. archival enabled false turns auto-archival off; an agent cannot turn it on: when it is off and enabled true is sent, nothing changes and the result gives the Automations page link for the user. The cleanup and archival responses list the changed fields and the settings as read back.

accountWide.description: For autoFlagging and autoReleasing; ignored when false with cleanup or archival. true changes account settings and rejects repo, githubRepoId, and projectKey. false changes one repository and requires repo or githubRepoId.

archival.description: Change this project's auto-archival. Send only the fields that change.

enabled.description: false turns automatic archival off. true only works when it is already on; turning it on needs a person on the Automations page.

graceSeconds.description: How long a ready flag waits before it is archived (1 hour to 30 days).

notifyMemberIds.description: Member IDs to notify about archival activity. Replaces the whole list.

notifyTeamKeys.description: Team keys to notify about archival activity. Replaces the whole list.

requireApproval.description: true creates an approval request instead of archiving directly.

watchCadenceSeconds.description: How often watched flags are rechecked.

approvalRequired.description: Whether auto-flagging pull requests need approval.

cleanup.description: Change this project's auto-cleanup. Send only the fields that change.

customContext.description: Extra instructions for the cleanup agent, such as where flags are defined. Replaces the stored text.

flagStates.description: Which flags runs pick up. Replaces the whole list. Defaults to readyToArchive.

maxJobsPerRun.description: Most cleanup pull requests one run opens.

repositories.description: GitHub repositories (owner/name) that cleanup opens pull requests in. Replaces the whole list.

retryAttempted.description: true retries flags that already had a cleanup pull request.

schedule.description: How often cleanup runs. disabled turns automated cleanup off.

githubRepoId.description: Numeric GitHub repository id, an alternative to repo.

projectKey.description: With cleanup or archival: the project whose settings change (required). With accountWide false: the LaunchDarkly project to map the repository to, required on the first map.

repo.description: One GitHub repository's auto-flagging and auto-releasing, as owner/name, for example launchdarkly/gonfalon. Not for cleanup or archival.

githubRepoId.description: Numeric GitHub repository id, an alternative to repo.

projectKey.description: Any LaunchDarkly project key, used to look up the account-wide GitHub App install. Defaults to the oldest project.

repo.description: One GitHub repository's auto-flagging and auto-releasing, as owner/name, for example launchdarkly/gonfalon. Not for cleanup or archival.

name: create-environment-release-plan
description:
Create an environment release plan, a reusable progressive-release recipe. Does not start a release on a flag. Check existing plans with get-environment-release-plans first: an active key returns 409. Beta API.

GATHERING CONFIG: ask the user about each setting as its own question, in its own step. Never bundle randomizationUnit, advancementMode and cleanupBehavior into one prompt or offer pre-mixed combinations. Ask (1) randomizationUnit: the context kind to randomize by (e.g. user, account); (2) advancementMode: manual or automatic; (3) cleanupBehavior: leave_rules_in_place or remove_rules_and_update_default_rule, stating each outcome. Then make one create call with the complete config.

progressiveRelease: randomizationUnit, optional advancementMode (manual or automatic, default manual) and cleanupBehavior, phases, and optional metrics. cleanupBehavior sets what happens when a release finishes: leave_rules_in_place keeps the rules, so the release stays limited to the audience in them; remove_rules_and_update_default_rule removes the rules and releases to everyone through the default rule (the API default).

PHASES: 1-10, each with 1-10 clauses and 1-10 steps. A flag release plan can use this plan only if it has exactly one phase. Every phase's clauses must include the randomization unit clause {attribute: "kind", op: "in", values: [<randomizationUnit>], contextKind: <randomizationUnit>}; alone it releases to every context of that kind. randomizationUnit must be an existing, unarchived context kind in the project. Clauses use the flag targeting shape {attribute, op, values, contextKind?, negate?}: contextKind defaults to user, and attribute and contextKind may be empty only for segmentMatch, whose values are segment keys. values holds 1-25 entries, each string at most 1,024 bytes.

STEPS: {allocation, durationMillis}. allocation is per-100k (5000 = 5%): greater than 0, at most 99000 (99%), and greater than the previous step's. Do not add a 100% step; completing the release reaches everyone. durationMillis is the hold before the next step and must be greater than 0 (14400000 = 4h).

METRICS: object keyed by metric or metric group key, each {isGroup, autoRollback?}. Empty makes a progressive release; any keys make releases from the plan guarded, which caps every step at 50000 (50%) and requires the randomizationUnit to be enabled for guarded rollouts. Max 10 metrics and 5 groups; keys must exist in the project and each metric must support the randomizationUnit.

One example per release type:
- progressive, no metrics: {"projectKey":"default","environmentKey":"production","key":"prod-ramp","name":"Production ramp","progressiveRelease":{"randomizationUnit":"user","advancementMode":"automatic","cleanupBehavior":"remove_rules_and_update_default_rule","phases":[{"clauses":[{"attribute":"kind","op":"in","values":["user"],"contextKind":"user"}],"steps":[{"allocation":10000,"durationMillis":3600000},{"allocation":50000,"durationMillis":3600000}]}]}}
- guarded, steps at most 50000: {"projectKey":"default","environmentKey":"production","key":"prod-guarded","name":"Production guarded","progressiveRelease":{"randomizationUnit":"user","advancementMode":"automatic","cleanupBehavior":"remove_rules_and_update_default_rule","phases":[{"clauses":[{"attribute":"kind","op":"in","values":["user"],"contextKind":"user"}],"steps":[{"allocation":10000,"durationMillis":3600000},{"allocation":50000,"durationMillis":3600000}]}],"metrics":{"error-rate":{"isGroup":false,"autoRollback":true}}}}

name: search-contexts
description:
Search for stored LaunchDarkly contexts in an environment by kind, key, or attribute value. Returns context records including their stored attributes (e.g., merchantCountryCode, disbursementRail) and when the context was last seen. Kind keys and attribute names differ per project: find them with get-context-kinds and get-context-attributes instead of guessing.

Convenience param:
- `kind`: filter to a specific context kind (e.g. `Merchant`, `user`, `organization`). Emitted as the filter clause `kind equals "<kind>"`.

Raw filter syntax (passed in `filter`) uses `field operator value` clauses. Operators: `equals`, `notEquals`, `anyOf`, `startsWith`, `exists`, `before`, `after`; `contains` and `notContains` are not supported. Combine clauses with `,` (AND) or `|` (OR); group with `()`. Supported fields: `kind`, `key`, `kindKey`, `applicationId`, `q`, `<kind>.<attribute>` for one kind's attribute, `*.<attribute>` for any kind, and bare `name` for `*.name`.

Attribute rules: only top-level attributes can be filtered, and the name must start with a letter or underscore followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`. Nested paths such as `user.address.city` and JSON pointers are rejected; find those contexts by kind or key and read their attributes with get-context-instances. A filter may hold at most 10 attribute clauses. `startsWith` is case-sensitive. `q` takes only `equals` with one non-empty string and prefix-matches the context key and the `name`, `firstName`, `lastName`, and `email` attributes.

Examples:
- `kind equals "Merchant"` — contexts of a specific kind
- `Merchant.merchantCountryCode equals "US"` — Merchant contexts whose attribute matches
- `key startsWith "merchant-"` — contexts whose key has a prefix
- `applicationId equals "GoSDK/1.2"` — contexts reported by a specific SDK/application

Example combining both params: set `kind=Merchant` and `filter=Merchant.disbursementRail equals "PIX"` to find Merchant contexts on the PIX rail.

Note: the contexts API cannot filter by which flag a context evaluated; there is no `flagEvaluated` field. Filter by kind, key, applicationId, or attribute values instead.

Ordering is fixed by the API; there is no sort parameter.

Pagination: responses include `totalCount`. When hasMore is true, pass continuationToken from the response to get the next page.

name: get-flag-release-plans
description: Get flag release plans, reusable templates that say how a flag is released across a project's environments. Beta API. Without flagReleasePlanKey: a page in creation order with totalCount; when hasMore is true, pass nextOffset as offset. With flagReleasePlanKey: one plan with its environments (environmentKey, triggerType, environmentReleasePlanKey or isImmediate), executionMode, applicationKeys, maintainer, default, and version. A maintainer reads as {kind: member, memberId, email} or {kind: team, key, name}; to send a team maintainer to update-flag-release-plan, use {kind: team, teamKey: <key>}. The plan with default: true is the project's default, suggested first when starting a release. A project with no stored plans has no default; create a plan with default: true. Flag release plans are project-wide; environment release plans (get-environment-release-plans) are the per-environment rollout recipes they point to.
